paper.citation: Nie, X. and Wager, S. (2021). Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Biometrika 108(2), 299-319. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asaa076.
paper.source_version: arXiv:1712.04912v4, 2020-08-06; publication metadata verified separately against Biometrika (2021 issue)
paper.source_locator: arXiv v4 PDF pp. 15-16, Section 6.1, unnumbered common generation equations and Setup A; p. 18 Figure 3 caption for d=6 and sigma=1. Author repository experiments_for_paper/run_simu.R lines 25-32, 75-77 and start.sh lines 3-6 at commit 6806396960e672214e2ef36e16c76bbb58ef9114

mechanism.name: ATE under Nie--Wager Setup A: nonlinear confounding and heterogeneous effects

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y=b(X)+(A-0.5)*tau(X)+epsilon; epsilon~Normal(0,1), independent of X and treatment randomization

sampling.dependence: iid across individuals; six independent Uniform(0,1) covariates within each individual

assumptions: Consistency Y=Y(A) and well-defined binary treatment interventions.
Independent identically distributed individuals; no interference.
Conditional exchangeability (Y(0),Y(1)) independent of A given X; independent assignment uniforms and outcome noise implement it.
Positivity 0.1 <= P(A=1|X) <= 0.9 on the registered support.
All required pretreatment confounders X1,X2 are observed; complete data and finite first moments.

properties.notes: X1,X2 affect propensity and treatment effect; X1-X5 affect baseline; X6 is inactive. sin(pi*X1*X2) is a nonlinear interaction; 2*(X3-0.5)^2 is nonlinear; A*(X1+X2)/2 produces treatment-covariate interactions. d=6,n=128 is not called high-dimensional confounding.

estimand.name: theta_ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)]
estimand.definition: Superpopulation average effect of A=1 versus A=0, under X~Uniform([0,1]^6). Not the realized-sample average effect, ATT, CATE output, or unadjusted observed group difference.

truth.expression: Superpopulation average effect of A=1 versus A=0, under X~Uniform([0,1]^6). Not the realized-sample average effect, ATT, CATE output, or unadjusted observed group difference.
truth.derivation: Analytic expectation E[(X1+X2)/2]=1/2; independently integrate separately implemented potential-outcome means with tensor Gauss-Legendre orders 3 and 5 in six dimensions.

adaptations: Retain Setup A equations and the d=6, sigma=1 parameter cell; rename source treatment W as A.
Collect the scalar population ATE E[Y(1)-Y(0)] instead of the source CATE function. The value 0.5 is derived here, not presented as a paper-reported ATE estimate.
Use Python/NumPy PCG64 and row-major X draws with independent uniform-threshold Bernoulli assignment; distributional reconstruction, not identical R random draws.
Use n=128, seed=1729 for a CPU interface check instead of the source estimator experiments. No estimator is fitted.
effect_scale=1 preserves the original treatment effect; zero and reversed values appear only in verification controls, not as additional registered families or scenarios.
